These define optimal resource allocation boundaries for Bayesian optimization. The efficient point identifies when marginal returns drop below a threshold δ_1, while the saturation point marks when performance plateaus within δ_2. This dual criterion replaces fixed-rung strategies like Hyperband’s successive halving, offering a more adaptive and budget-efficient approach. The method assumes smooth, monotonic learning curves, but may fail under noisy or discontinuous performance profiles. For GSE, these primitives enable dynamic state transitions in HPO, allowing real-time adjustment of seasonal budgets based on observed convergence behavior. The mapping to GSI involves using these points to inform Bayesian posterior updates with calibrated confidence intervals. The failure mode occurs when early observations misrepresent true learning dynamics, particularly in models with abrupt performance shifts such as gradient boosting trees.
